data/goods.json, visitors.json, market.json (hourly rates, weather weights and W, rent, start coins), upgrades.json (prices), stamps.json (thresholds) are read by dm_game.py; README says how to change a good, a visitor type, an upgrade or a stamp (and admits that upgrade/stamp effects and the six-good count are in code).

f_stall.png: 6x2 grid, back row above front, crates lettered and coloured per good (fish blue F, flowers pink F), yellow cursor outline at (1,1) as in the state, GOOD: APPLES, PRICE: 4, CRATES: 8 OF 8.

f_day.png / f_q.png: stall with crates, aisle row with visitors at their cells (C34 at x2, T33 at x4, coloured by type), queue showing T and B tokens, TILL 1 R13, and time, speed, coins, taken, served, walked out, reputation.

Viewed title, slots, settings, morning, upgrades, paused, evening, season over frames: all texts drawn (in capitals), chosen entry marked with > and yellow (title New season, settings Difficulty, morning Fish row, upgrades Second till, paused Resume).
README gives play keys, headless and frame commands (both ran as written), and says everything kept is in the --store folder (settings.json, slots.json, stamps.json, records.json).

defects: The headless run prints the JSON with ensure_ascii=False through the console code page, so on this machine Spanish texts (Español, Día, Mañana) come out cp1252, not UTF-8, when stdout is piped; a UTF-8 reader fails to decode it.
The frame font has capitals only, so every text is drawn upper case (MORNING, APPLES) rather than as the strings read.
Spanish uses Mañana both for the Morning heading and the Tomorrow: line.
Adding a seventh good needs code changes (the draws and next_good use 6), as the README admits; upgrade and stamp effects are code, only their numbers are data.
Window mode (--play, tkinter) was not run by the builder or by me.
